battery.beats_random: Welch t vs random entries >= 2.0 (20 draws)
battery.costs_stress: mean R > 0 with spread x1.5, slippage x2, commission and swap x1.5
battery.delay_stress: mean R > 0 with entry one bar late
battery.instruments: >= 60% of instruments with >= 20 trades positive (>= 2 instruments)
battery.leave_one_out: mean R > 0 with any one instrument removed
battery.outliers: top 5% of trades carry < 50% of total R
battery.perturbation: mean R > 0 with tercile edges moved by -0.05 and +0.05 quantile
battery.regimes: no regime cell (er120 x vol_ratio, discovery medians) with t <= -2.0; >= 2 cells with >= 20 trades positive
battery.years: >= 60% of years with >= 20 trades positive (>= 2 years)

costs.status: slippage, commission and swap are declared approximations
costs.swap: 0.01 x ATR24(D1) per New York close crossed

spec.decision_bar: the first D1 bar closing at or after the release; none if the next report is already public
spec.entry: market order at the open of the bar after the decision bar (= the decision bar's close)

exit.rule: time exit after 5 D1 bars (the next decision bar's close), protective stop 2.0 x ATR24(D1); 1R = the stop distance; no target

gates.confirmation_2016: computed only for PROMISING-or-better: 2016 mean R > 0 and > 0 under the cost stress
gates.incremental: judged mean R minus the declared price-only control's judged mean R > 0; for the veto: the uncrowded trend control's mean minus the trend control's mean > 0
gates.top5_removed: judged mean R > 0 without the 5 best trades

holdout.pass: 2016-2017 pooled mean > 0 with clustered t >= 1.645, 2017 alone mean > 0, and 2016-2017 mean > 0 under the cost stress
holdout.policy: RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md section 2: one preregistered final test of ONE candidate that passed everything else; the best such by judged t; never for a PROMISING one

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: a crowded speculative position has few marginal buyers (sellers) left and unwinds
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk; Tornell & Yuan, Speculation and hedging in the currency futures markets: are they informative to the spot exchange rates?, Journal of Futures Markets 32 (2012): examines whether turning points of net positions are informative
hypotheses.statement: When Leveraged Money's net position (as a share of open interest) is at a 52-week extreme (percentile >= 0.90 or <= 0.10), trading the currency AGAINST it for one week (D3) has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: continuation: speculators trade on information or trends that persist beyond the report
hypotheses.sources: Klitgaard & Weir, Exchange rate changes and net positions of speculators in the futures market, FRBNY Economic Policy Review 10 (2004): weekly position CHANGES move with same-week exchange rates; little evidence that they predict later moves; Tornell & Yuan, Speculation and hedging in the currency futures markets: are they informative to the spot exchange rates?, Journal of Futures Markets 32 (2012): examines whether turning points of net positions are informative
hypotheses.statement: When Leveraged Money's net position is at a 52-week extreme, trading the currency WITH it for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: a stretched price that is also crowded has the least support left
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk
hypotheses.statement: When positioning AND the currency's price are both at a same-side 52-week extreme, trading against them for one week has positive net expectancy -- and more than the price extreme alone.

hypotheses.mechanism: continuation: positioning confirms that the price extreme is a trend, not noise
hypotheses.sources: Klitgaard & Weir, Exchange rate changes and net positions of speculators in the futures market, FRBNY Economic Policy Review 10 (2004): weekly position CHANGES move with same-week exchange rates; little evidence that they predict later moves
hypotheses.statement: When positioning and price are both at a same-side 52-week extreme, trading with them for one week has positive net expectancy -- and more than the price extreme alone.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: positioning information that price has not shown (the pure positioning effect)
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk
hypotheses.statement: When positioning is at a 52-week extreme but price is NOT at the same-side extreme, trading against the positioning for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: continuation: speculators position ahead of a move that price has not yet made
hypotheses.sources: Tornell & Yuan, Speculation and hedging in the currency futures markets: are they informative to the spot exchange rates?, Journal of Futures Markets 32 (2012): examines whether turning points of net positions are informative
hypotheses.statement: When positioning is at a 52-week extreme but price is not, trading with the positioning for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: continuation: position building reflects information that is still being priced
hypotheses.sources: Klitgaard & Weir, Exchange rate changes and net positions of speculators in the futures market, FRBNY Economic Policy Review 10 (2004): weekly position CHANGES move with same-week exchange rates; little evidence that they predict later moves
hypotheses.statement: When the 4-week change in Leveraged Money's net position is at a 52-week extreme, trading with the flow for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: a burst of position building overshoots and is given back
hypotheses.sources: Klitgaard & Weir, Exchange rate changes and net positions of speculators in the futures market, FRBNY Economic Policy Review 10 (2004): weekly position CHANGES move with same-week exchange rates; little evidence that they predict later moves
hypotheses.statement: When the 4-week positioning change is at a 52-week extreme, trading against the flow for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: the unwind of a crowded position has started and is self-reinforcing
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk; Tornell & Yuan, Speculation and hedging in the currency futures markets: are they informative to the spot exchange rates?, Journal of Futures Markets 32 (2012): examines whether turning points of net positions are informative
hypotheses.statement: When positioning is at a 52-week extreme AND last week's change points back toward neutral, trading against the positioning for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: in stress, funding constraints force crowded positions to unwind
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk
hypotheses.statement: When positioning is at a 52-week extreme while VIX >= 20, trading against the positioning for one week has positive net expectancy.

hypotheses.mechanism: reversal: a crowded trend is the one most likely to stall; filtering it improves the price strategy
hypotheses.sources: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen, Carry trades and currency crashes, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 23 (2008): speculators' net futures positions in carry currencies relate to future crash risk
hypotheses.statement: Taking the 13-week trend trade where positioning is ALREADY at an extreme in the trend's direction LOSES (negative net expectancy): positioning works as a veto on a price strategy.

lookback.normalisation: percentile rank (ties half) among the previous 52 weeks' reports; z-score only as a robustness variant

not_tested_here: asset-manager and dealer positioning as signals (reported descriptively)
spec.positioning: Leveraged Money long minus short (spreads excluded) / open interest; the currency future's own orientation (+ = bullish the currency)
spec.publication: 17:00 New York on the first weekday >= as-of + 6 days; 2013-10-01..2013-12-24 dropped
spec.question: Does CFTC positioning (Leveraged Money, TFF futures-only) predict the direction of the seven direct USD pairs over the following week, after costs, out of sample -- and does it add anything beyond a price-only rule with the same timing, exit and costs?
robustness_reported: z-score definition at the same normal quantiles
costs x2 (spread x2, slippage x4, commission and swap x2)
by instrument, year, regime; entry one bar late (battery)

rules.a_cont: CONTROL: price at a 52-week extreme: trade with it
rules.a_rev: CONTROL: price at a 52-week extreme of its weekly samples: trade against it
rules.a_trend: CONTROL: trade the sign of the 13-week (65-bar) trend at every decision
rules.a_trend_uncrowded: CONTROL: the 13-week trend trade except where positioning is at an extreme in the trend's direction
rules.af_cont: CONTROL: 4-week price change at a 52-week extreme: trade with it
rules.af_rev: CONTROL: 4-week price change at a 52-week extreme: trade against it
rules.av_rev: CONTROL: price at a 52-week extreme while VIX >= 20: trade against it
rules.c_cont: positioning AND price both at a same-side 52-week extreme: trade with them
rules.c_rev: positioning AND price both at a same-side 52-week extreme: trade against them
rules.f_cont: 4-week change of Leveraged Money net/OI at a 52-week extreme: trade WITH the flow
rules.f_rev: 4-week positioning change at a 52-week extreme: trade AGAINST the flow
rules.i_cont: positioning at an extreme while price is not: trade with the positioning
rules.i_rev: positioning at an extreme while price is NOT at the same-side extreme: trade against the positioning
rules.p_cont: Leveraged Money net/OI at a 52-week extreme: trade WITH it
rules.p_rev: Leveraged Money net/OI at a 52-week extreme (pct >= 0.90 / <= 0.10): trade AGAINST it
rules.u_rev: positioning at an extreme AND last week's change points back (the unwind has started): trade against the positioning
rules.v_rev: positioning at an extreme while VIX >= 20: trade against the positioning
rules.x_veto: the 13-week trend trade taken where positioning is already at an extreme in the trend's direction (crowded)

status.PROMISING: judged mean > 0, clustered t >= 2.0, cost stress and beats-random pass, every gate passes (edges.judged_status), and the 2016 confirmation passes
status.VALIDATED: every battery check at the registry threshold, no blocking board objection, every gate, the 2016 confirmation, then the sealed holdout

spec.walk_forward: fixed rules: each calendar year is an out-of-sample fold; plus a descriptive walk-forward of SELECTION: in each year 2010..2015 trade the opportunity hypothesis with the best judged mean over all earlier years (>= 30 trades); no verdict depends on it
